name: DrivingStereo: High-Resolution Stereo Matching Dataset
description: Large-scale stereo matching and depth estimation dataset comprising 182,182 rectified binocular image pairs (1752x800 resolution) captured in diverse driving conditions with high-precision LiDAR-derived ground truth disparity maps and adverse weather subsets.

license.name: MIT License
license.notes: Released under the permissive MIT license.

source_references.title: DrivingStereo Official Website
source_references.notes: Official dataset project page providing download links for full and half resolution stereo pairs, disparity maps, and weather subsets.

source_references.title: DrivingStereo: A Large-Scale Dataset for Stereo Matching in Autonomous Driving Scenarios
source_references.notes: CVPR 2019 conference publication by Yang et al. detailing the stereo camera rig, LiDAR-guided disparity ground truth generation, and model evaluations.

verification.notes: Verified against official DrivingStereo project page and CVPR 2019 proceedings (DOI: 10.1109/CVPR.2019.00099).

size.notes: Exact aggregate byte size is not published as a single figure by the authors; dataset is distributed as 38 training sequence zips, 4 testing sequence zips, and weather-specific subsets in full and half resolution.

citation.paper_title: DrivingStereo: A Large-Scale Dataset for Stereo Matching in Autonomous Driving Scenarios

provenance.collection_method: Captured with a roof-mounted binocular stereo camera rig (1752x800 resolution) synchronized with a 64-beam rotating LiDAR sensor across 42 diverse driving sequences.
provenance.curation_notes: Ground-truth disparity is generated through a multi-frame LiDAR point cloud integration and occlusion-aware filtering pipeline. Includes specialized adverse weather subsets covering rain, fog, dusk, and highway scenarios.
